instruction.text: Place all the objects into the box with their front sides facing left.

semantic_contract: All four objects must be inside the box, down on its bottom, each lying with its length along the box's long direction.

Each object's front end must point toward world -X, the robot's own left and the side of the table where the left arm is mounted, with its back end toward world +X. This is what the instruction means by front sides facing left; the direction is fixed in the world and does not change with the camera view.

The front end is the car's nose, the electric toothbrush's brush-head end, the hammer's head end and the shoe's toe. The back end is the car's rear, the bottom end of the toothbrush handle, the free end of the hammer's handle and the shoe's heel.
The box must stay upright with its long direction running along world X.
Both arms must be back at the poses they held when the episode reset, at the same instant that everything else in this contract is true.

review_notes: All four item groups are required: _combined_item_score_options(4)[0].
Box metadata longest horizontal dimension is local Y; object/checkpoint heading alignment describes orientation, not a row of object positions.
World +X is disclosed only as the task language direction convention, not an object pose or numeric evaluator tolerance. Camera-image left is not this fixed task direction.
get_score open-gripper conditions and partial-score levels are not Boolean success criteria.
Point-in-functional-box is a proxy for bottom-interior placement, not a containment or stable-support certificate.

v3: the heading checks align the checkpoint -X (shoe: root +X) with world +X, and the mesh probe shows that axis points at the handle, heel or rear end in every selectable variant. The front end (head, brush head, toe, nose) therefore points toward world -X, the robot's own left. Registry-v4's '+X front' was the reverse under the natural meaning of front; functional_axis_review now records the checked end and the front end separately.

changes: Defines each object's front and back end publicly by shape: the car's nose and rear, the electric toothbrush's brush-head end and the bottom end of its handle, the hammer's head end and the free end of its handle, the shoe's toe and heel. Registry-v4 used 'front' without defining it for the toothbrush or the hammer.

Reverses the stated direction to match the pinned checks. Each item check aligns one object axis with world +X: the checkpoint frame's -X for the car, toothbrush and hammer, the root +X for the shoe. In every selectable variant that axis points at the bottom of the toothbrush handle, the free end of the hammer handle and the shoe's heel, and at the car's rear, so the natural front end must point toward world -X, the robot's own left; that is also the plain reading of 'front sides facing left'. Registry-v4 (and the v2 layer before it) told the policy the front points toward world +X; the v2 review's front_axis entries named the checked axis as the front, and that identification is withdrawn here.

Pins env/scene_manager/layout_manager.py and utils/transformer.py as evaluator dependencies: the checked heading is composed through get_functional_points and pose_to_matrix, so fresh preflight now refuses drift in either, as the other RoboDojo records already do.
